needs: Record daily habits quickly on phone and desktop with repeated timed events.
Associate a tracking day and its after-midnight events with the appropriate following main night.
Export collected data for later comparison with Garmin outside the MVP.
context: Round 1 and round 2 user edits are preserved in docs/mvp-answers-round-1.md and docs/mvp-answers-round-2.md. docs/mvp-questions.md consolidates them and the four subsequent chat confirmations.
Confirmed: open email/password registration with private per-account data; online-only quick capture; separate repeated drink intakes and reusable favorites.
Confirmed: strict 04:00 Europe/Paris tracking-day boundary with manual night reassignment. Habitual 23:30–07:00 is informational only and never changes assignment or creates sleep measurements.
Confirmed: green tea, black tea, mate and infusions with volume; one activity type per session with intensity, start and duration; naps start/duration.

Confirmed: independent daily alcohol/gluten yes/no; dinner time plus small/medium/big/massive quantity; manual late-sugar yes/no plus time when present; non-caffeinated evening drink yes/no; cat presence only.
Confirmed: separate experienced tracking-day stress and anticipated next-day stress, each absent/medium/high; planned early-wake constraint with target time and reason; unrestricted past corrections.
Confirmed: a private free-text feature-suggestion control near every action, with an in-app suggestion list and no automatic GitHub publication. Suggestions are separate from health journal events.

Implementation defaults explicitly documented: volume in ml; initial activity types walking/running/cycling/strength/other; intensity low/medium/high; fixed drink catalog; versioned JSON and CSV all-history export; no special travel mode.
User delegates stack selection: React/TypeScript, FastAPI, SQLite and Docker. Public source only; no personal records or credentials. Hosting integration remains a later operational step.

Excluded: offline writes, mandatory recap, generic custom factors, mixed-ingredient drinks, reminders, manual sleep measurements, cat awakening metrics, Garmin integration, correlation and production deployment.
acceptance_criteria: AC1: Deliver an authenticated French mobile-first installable online-only PWA with quick event buttons, open email/password registration and server-persisted records shared across devices; enforce per-account isolation and truthful failed/offline saves without an offline queue.

AC2: Preserve actual timestamps/offsets, tracking dates and stable editable nominal night IDs; apply the strict 04:00 Europe/Paris boundary including 05:00, midnight, DST and manual overrides; habitual 23:30–07:00 is informational and never measured or used to override assignment.

AC3: Support separate repeated timed green tea, black tea, mate and infusion intakes with positive volume in ml and reusable favorites creating independent entries; evening non-caffeinated drink is a separate yes/no/unknown context flag, not an inferred or duplicated intake.

AC4: Support repeated activity sessions with exactly one type, low/medium/high intensity, start and positive duration; support naps with start plus positive duration and validate interval consistency.

AC5: Capture dinner time plus small/medium/big/massive quantity, independent daily alcohol/gluten yes/no/unknown, and manual late-sugar yes/no/unknown plus time when yes; no automatic late threshold or alcohol quantity is required.

AC6: Capture cat presence only, separate experienced tracking-day and anticipated next-day stress at absent/medium/high, and a planned early-wake constraint with target time and reason; preserve unknown answers and never overwrite anticipation with later experienced stress.

AC7: Provide unrestricted past create/edit/delete history and fixed factors without a mandatory recap; place a private free-text feature-suggestion control near every action and provide an owner-only suggestion list, separate from journal events and without GitHub publication.

AC8: Export all history in versioned JSON and a normalized CSV bundle with stable IDs, actual timestamps/offsets, units, missingness, dinner quantity, intensity, distinct stress periods, tracking days and editable nominal night links; include favorites and suggestions in separately identified sections/files and verify completeness with synthetic fixtures.

AC9: Keep Garmin imports/synchronization/credentials, correlations, recommendations, manual sleep metrics, reminders, cat awakening metrics and automatic GitHub issue creation outside the MVP; document future external Garmin joins without fabricating sleep intervals.

AC10: Provide reproducible local startup, a container artifact, persistent storage and documented backup/restore for the retained stack; verify registration and cross-account read/write/delete/export/suggestion isolation with synthetic data; do not deploy production as part of planning.

product.title: SommeilEnOr personal sleep context journal
product.overview: A fast French PWA to collect daily and nightly context and export it for later sleep analysis.
goals: Fast online-only quick-action capture with reusable favorites, unrestricted corrections and isolated accounts.
Reliable temporal links across midnight and devices.
Complete portable records with explicit missingness.
non_goals: Correlation dashboards, causal claims or health recommendations.
Production deployment during initial corpus creation.
Offline writes or synchronization, reminders, manual sleep metrics, mixed-drink composition and a generic custom-factor builder.

backlog_items.title: Define tracking days nights and collection data contracts
problem: Midnight and ambiguous missing values can make future sleep comparisons incorrect.
scope_in: Use strict 04:00 Europe/Paris day assignment including events during nocturnal awakenings; manual override remains available.
Define nominal nights without measured sleep data, dinner quantity enum, stress periods, intensity, favorite identity and separate private feature suggestions.
Preserve original timestamps/offsets and missingness; habitual 23:30–07:00 is informational only.
Priority rationale: temporal identity and missingness are dependencies of every capture screen.
scope_out: Garmin integration, correlations and production deployment.
acceptance_criteria: AC1: Specify 00:30, 03:59, 04:00, 05:00 and 08:00 assignment plus DST/offset preservation and manual override; habitual hours have no assignment effect.
AC2: Define separate experienced tracking-day and anticipated next-day stress fields, each absent/medium/high with unknown distinct from absent.
AC3: Define dinner quantity, intensity, positive volume/duration, timed late-sugar validation, owner IDs, favorites and private suggestion contracts in the full export schema.

backlog_items.title: Build authenticated cross-device PWA foundation
problem: A public repository must deliver a private journal usable across devices.
scope_in: Open email/password registration, per-account sessions and isolated private server persistence using the selected stack.
French responsive quick-action shell, HTTPS installability and service worker updates without journal write caching.
Visible pending/saved/failed/disconnected states; no offline queue or automatic replay.
Owner-scoped authorization for events, context, favorites, suggestions and exports; duplicate registration and credential errors are handled safely.
Priority rationale: access control and reliable persistence precede personal-data collection.
scope_out: Garmin integration, correlations and production deployment.
acceptance_criteria: AC1: Register two accounts and verify unauthenticated access fails and neither account can read/mutate/delete/export the other account data, favorites or suggestions, including guessed IDs.
AC2: Demonstrate a saved record is visible on a second browser of the same account and layouts work on mobile/desktop.
AC3: Verify HTTPS installability/updates and failed/offline save states; no offline entry is silently queued or replayed.

backlog_items.title: Collect repeated beverages physical activities and naps
problem: Repeated daily events cannot be represented by one boolean per category.
scope_in: Fixed green tea/black tea/mate/infusion catalog, intake time and volume in ml; separate repeated entries and reusable favorites.
Favorites copy selected values into fresh independently editable entries; a new intake uses its own timestamp, never the favorite creation timestamp.
One activity type per session with start, positive duration and low/medium/high intensity; start-plus-duration naps.
Initial activity options walking/running/cycling/strength/other are editable implementation defaults; no mixed sessions or custom factor builder.
Evening non-caffeinated drink is a separate yes/no/unknown context flag; an infusion intake is not duplicated.
Priority rationale: timed repeated events are the core collection workflow.
scope_out: Garmin integration, correlations and production deployment.
acceptance_criteria: AC1: Save repeated tea/mate/infusion intakes with time/positive ml volume and use a favorite to create a fresh entry without overwriting prior records.
AC2: Save repeatable single-type activities with intensity and start/duration plus naps; reject invalid quantities and preserve manual night overrides.
AC3: Keep evening non-caffeinated yes/no/unknown independent of caffeinated intake and never create a duplicate infusion event.

backlog_items.title: Collect meal night context and daily assessments
problem: Meal and night context needs clear granularity and meaningful unanswered states.
scope_in: Dinner time plus small/medium/big/massive portion size; independent daily alcohol/gluten yes/no/unknown.
Manual late sugar yes/no/unknown plus time when yes, without a derived threshold; non-caffeinated evening drink yes/no/unknown.
Night cat presence only, separate experienced/anticipated three-level stress, planned early-wake constraint with target time/reason.
Feature-suggestion button near each action opens private free text stored separately from journal entries; provide an owner-only list without external sending.
Priority rationale: complete the requested factor set after shared capture patterns exist.
scope_out: Garmin integration, correlations and production deployment.
Manual sleep metrics, actual awakenings, reminders, generic custom factors and automatic GitHub issue creation.
acceptance_criteria: AC1: Independently create/correct dinner time and portion, alcohol/gluten, timed sugar, evening drink and cat answers; distinguish missing from explicit no.
AC2: Save experienced tracking-day and anticipated next-day stress separately; planned early waking stores target time/reason without recording actual wake measurements.
AC3: Open a suggestion control from each action, store its action context and private text, and list it for its owner only; it creates no journal event or external issue.

backlog_items.title: Deliver day night history and portable exports
problem: The collection MVP must already produce reliable inputs for later external comparisons.
scope_in: Unrestricted historical create/edit/delete and day/night navigation without a mandatory recap.
All-history versioned JSON and normalized CSV with a data dictionary; negative and unknown values remain distinct.
Preserve dinner portion, activity intensity, timed sugar, independent stress periods, raw timestamps and night overrides.
Include favorites and private suggestions in distinct export sections/files, never as journal events.
Future Garmin matching uses nominal night date and stored offsets, not fabricated wake times.
Priority rationale: useful history and lossless export complete the collection promise.
scope_out: Garmin integration, correlations and production deployment.
acceptance_criteria: AC1: Compare every persisted synthetic entity/relationship to JSON and CSV export, including repeated events, portion/intensity, timed sugar, stress, favorites, suggestions, midnight/DST and missing/negative answers.
AC2: Historical corrections and explicit night overrides remain consistent in history and export, without requiring sleep measurements.
AC3: Exports are owner-only, omit credentials and contain no fabricated Garmin/correlation fields; suggestions stay in a separate section/file.

backlog_items.title: Package and verify collection MVP for self hosting
problem: A cross-device journal needs reproducible operations and recoverable persistent storage.
scope_in: Use React/TypeScript + FastAPI + SQLite/Docker; verify open registration and cross-account isolation of the online-only app.
Document local startup and selected dependency versions, container build and generic HTTPS reverse-proxy integration.
Use environment templates without real deployment addresses or credentials.
Document and exercise backup/restore with synthetic data and persistent volumes.
Focused integration and responsive-browser checks; French i18n contract validation.
Priority rationale: operational verification is required before any later deployment.
scope_out: Garmin integration, correlations and production deployment.
acceptance_criteria: AC1: Start a clean instance from documented commands and verify a restart preserves synthetic journal entries.
AC2: Restore a two-account synthetic backup into an isolated instance; compare journal, favorites, suggestions and exports and verify ownership isolation remains intact.
AC3: Run the relevant automated checks and mobile/desktop smoke checks; record evidence without claiming production deployment.

orchestration_task.title: Orchestrate SommeilEnOr collection MVP delivery
plan: Use the consolidated round 1/2 decisions and chat confirmations in docs/mvp-questions.md; implement the existing prioritized slices with documented editable defaults, without reopening answered questions.
Deliver High-priority temporal/data contracts first, then authenticated PWA foundation.
Deliver High-priority repeated events, meal/night assessments, then history and full export.
Deliver Medium-priority packaging and restore verification after the functional slices.
Record evidence against each request AC, run appropriate checks and Logics validation, and close out only after actual implementation; deployment needs a separate instruction.
